title: Q3 - Second-highest distinct salary
summary: SQL / SQL / Window functions / Ties and partitions

children.text: Classic SQL screener: how would you return the second-highest distinct salary, and how do ROW_NUMBER, RANK and DENSE_RANK differ?

items: Clarify distinct salary value versus second employee row.
Use DENSE_RANK for distinct values without gaps.
Add PARTITION BY department_id for the follow-up.

children.text: DENSE_RANK over salary descending assigns consecutive ranks to distinct salary values. ROW_NUMBER numbers individual rows; tied rows need a tie-breaker for deterministic row selection. RANK shares a rank across ties and leaves gaps. Filter null salaries explicitly.
For a single global value, MAX below the overall MAX also works and returns NULL if there is no second value.

children.title: Watch for this
children.text: ROW_NUMBER = 2 can return the highest salary again when two employees tie. RANK = 2 may not exist after a first-place tie.

items: How would you return the second-highest distinct salary within each department?
